occurrences.status: Displays the outlet key and offers a rope while mistaking the injured youth for a corpse.

occurrences.title: All the Money and a Strip of Cloth
occurrences.status: Searches both men, conceals a strip of coat and takes all the coins.

occurrences.title: The Gate Opened and Closed
occurrences.status: Inspects the shore, unlocks the grating and relocks it after the men pass.

occurrences.title: An Unrecognized Visitor
occurrences.status: Enters in threadbare black, green spectacles, a high cravat and flattened gray hair, bowing over an old hat.

occurrences.title: A Secret for Sale
occurrences.status: Performs his disguised role and lowers the price of his information.

occurrences.title: Thénardier Unmasked
occurrences.status: Takes the note, removes spectacles and nose-quills, and admits his name.

occurrences.title: The Accusations Reversed
occurrences.status: Explains the shared identity and suicide, then unfolds the printed evidence.

occurrences.title: The Printed Proofs
occurrences.status: Has supplied the two newspaper proofs that overturn the supposed theft and murder.

occurrences.title: The Supposed Corpse
occurrences.status: Describes the burden as a murder victim and holds up the bloodied coat fragment.

occurrences.title: The Coat Fits
occurrences.status: Pockets the notes and leaves bewildered but pleased.

occurrences.title: The Morning Separation
occurrences.status: Meets the departing mother and reports how bitterly she is crying in the street.

occurrences.title: A Cry Elsewhere in the House
A Gold Piece in the Wooden Shoe
The Address Lost in the Wind
Come Along, Young Ones
occurrences.status: Enters with his brother and later says they have nowhere to sleep.

occurrences.title: The Shawl Given Away
occurrences.status: Keeps close behind the guide with his brother.

occurrences.title: A Sou of White Bread
occurrences.status: Describes their lost household and eats the offered bread.

occurrences.title: Montparnasse in Blue Spectacles
occurrences.status: Follows into shelter holding his brother’s hand.

occurrences.title: The Elephant Address
occurrences.status: Watches the altered face with dawning amusement.

occurrences.title: The Ladder Between the Forelegs
occurrences.status: Climbs hesitantly and helps receive his little brother.

occurrences.title: A Light in the Wooden Skeleton
occurrences.status: Enters the sleeping enclosure and asks about its purpose.

occurrences.title: Thunder Over the Roof
occurrences.status: Questions the guide and notices the fire risk.

occurrences.title: The Hand Against the Rats
occurrences.status: Sleeps between the two as the protected bed holds.

occurrences.title: The Son Goes Back to the Children
The Boys Who Did Not Return
The Lost Brothers in the Garden
occurrences.status: Leads his brother by the hand while carrying a small stick.

occurrences.title: Behind the Swan-Hutch
occurrences.status: Keeps with his brother behind the green swan-hutch.

occurrences.title: Compassion for the Swans
occurrences.status: Waits near the basin while the prosperous pair withdraws.

occurrences.title: The Larger Share
occurrences.status: Leans over the curb, retrieves the wet brioche with his stick and takes the smaller share.

occurrences.title: The Address Lost in the Wind
Come Along, Young Ones
occurrences.status: Cries as the barber rejects them and follows his brother.

occurrences.title: The Shawl Given Away
occurrences.status: Follows through the street and rain.

occurrences.title: A Sou of White Bread
occurrences.status: Eats his share with the others.

occurrences.title: Montparnasse in Blue Spectacles
occurrences.status: Stays with his brother during the adult conversation.

occurrences.title: The Elephant Address
occurrences.status: Looks back at the man he takes for Punchinello.

occurrences.title: The Ladder Between the Forelegs
occurrences.status: Is pushed and pulled inside after being set on the ladder.

occurrences.title: A Light in the Wooden Skeleton
occurrences.status: Clings to his brother and begins to feel warm under the blanket.

occurrences.title: Thunder Over the Roof
occurrences.status: Starts up in fright at the thunder before being settled again.

occurrences.title: The Hand Against the Rats
occurrences.status: Fears the rats until the offered hand calms him.

occurrences.title: The Son Goes Back to the Children
The Boys Who Did Not Return
The Lost Brothers in the Garden
occurrences.status: Walks beside his brother and says he is hungry.

occurrences.title: Behind the Swan-Hutch
occurrences.status: Repeats his hunger while watching the approaching pair.

occurrences.title: Compassion for the Swans
occurrences.status: Remains hungry beside his brother.

occurrences.title: The Larger Share
occurrences.status: Receives the larger portion from his brother.

occurrences.title: Ten Louis and a Commission
occurrences.status: Explains his transfer and diligence route and accepts the spying commission.

occurrences.title: The Watcher Sleeps
occurrences.status: Sleeps through his watch and recalls the commission at the relay.

occurrences.title: Flowers for a Supposed Rendezvous
occurrences.status: Follows from curiosity and continues interpreting the errand as a romance.

occurrences.title: The Bouquet on the Grave
occurrences.status: Discovers the grave that disproves the supposed romantic rendezvous.

occurrences.title: The Newspaper and the Visit
occurrences.status: Arrives in civilian clothes and greets the older man.

occurrences.title: Agreement Is Not Enough
occurrences.status: Agrees repeatedly and proposes limiting reading to official publications.

occurrences.title: The Writer She Recognizes
occurrences.status: Passes the gate and smiles, unaware of her changed response.

occurrences.title: Home with the Guests
occurrences.status: Attends his cousin’s wedding as a captain from Chartres without recognizing the bride.

occurrences.title: A Plan Kept Between the Men
occurrences.status: Takes his companions aside, raises the promised surprise, and lowers his voice to propose its undisclosed form.

occurrences.title: Under the Chestnut Trees
occurrences.status: Follows with a costly rattan and a cigar, presiding over the party’s amusement.

occurrences.title: The Swing at Issy
occurrences.status: Arranges the hire of asses, then sings the Spanish ballad while pushing the swing.

occurrences.title: Across the River and Down the Slopes
occurrences.status: Answers the repeated demand with a request for patience.

occurrences.title: Dinner at Bombarda’s
occurrences.status: Shares the restaurant table with Fantine and the other three couples.

occurrences.title: An Adoration for the Table
occurrences.status: Drinks while Favourite performs her declaration of love.

occurrences.title: An Appeal to Moderation
occurrences.status: Regains the noisy table’s attention with a pun and lectures on limits to wit, appetite, and desire.

occurrences.title: A Toast and a Mistaken Embrace
occurrences.status: Renounces his own prudence, toasts mirth, and embraces Favourite when he has called for Fantine.

occurrences.title: Restaurant Philosophy
occurrences.status: Answers philosophy with Désaugiers and turns praise of the restaurant into an oration on Aspasia.

occurrences.title: The Mare on the Quay
occurrences.status: Ends his interrupted speech with a punning strophe on the fallen mare.

occurrences.title: The Men Take Their Leave
occurrences.status: Announces the moment has arrived and directs the farewell kisses to the brow.

occurrences.title: Four Women in the Doorway
occurrences.status: Stands with the other portresses during the doorway conversation about animals and prices.

occurrences.title: What Do You Mean by Politics?
occurrences.status: Joins the women’s collective outcry at the child.

occurrences.title: Four Women in the Doorway
occurrences.status: Hears the rag-picker explain her trade before the child interrupts the doorway gathering.

occurrences.title: What Do You Mean by Politics?
occurrences.status: Adds to the collective abuse directed at Gavroche.

occurrences.title: An Extra Horse and a Guide
occurrences.status: Rides on the cart’s shaft to guide the traveller through the crossroads with an extra horse.

occurrences.title: A Branch for the Broken Whiffle-Tree
occurrences.status: Suggests returning when the fitting breaks, then drives on and predicts arrival at eight.

occurrences.title: A Road Barred Beyond Tinques
occurrences.status: Explains the longer route through Carency and Camblin and advises how to attempt it in darkness.

occurrences.title: The Dentist’s Offer
occurrences.status: Calls Fantine fortunate to be offered two napoleons for her teeth.

occurrences.title: The Pavilion and the Rear Lodge
The Clothes and the Quiet Door
Toussaint’s Reassurance Goes Astray
occurrences.status: Describes frightening hypothetical intruders and checks the house with her.

occurrences.title: Caresses and a False Report
occurrences.status: Spreads linen to dry in the pavilion’s attic, where her moving light is visible above the trees.

occurrences.title: Dinner and an Unheard Warning
occurrences.status: Sets the meal and repeatedly reports fighting in Paris.

occurrences.title: Which Quarter?
occurrences.status: Names the direction of Saint-Merry in answer to his question.

occurrences.title: A Pause Before the Lady
occurrences.status: Paces in front of his glittering stall while the child gazes.

occurrences.title: The Dentist’s Offer
occurrences.status: Offers one napoleon per upper front tooth and names the Tillac d’Argent as his evening address.

occurrences.title: The Unknown Gray-Haired Recruit
occurrences.status: Joins the band with a bold bearing noticed by the leaders.

occurrences.title: The Recruit at Work, the Visitor Gone
The Man in the Darkest Corner
occurrences.status: Sits at the least-lit table with a large musket between his legs.

occurrences.title: A Scout’s Warning
occurrences.status: Remains at the table as the porters take position.

occurrences.title: A Traveller Enters D——
occurrences.status: Enters on foot, drinks twice, and salutes the unresponsive gendarme after leaving the town-hall.

occurrences.title: A Place by the Kitchen Fire
occurrences.status: Shows his purse and waits by the fire, unaware that the innkeeper is checking his identity.

occurrences.title: The Name on the Reply
occurrences.status: Looks at the town-hall reply and leaves with his head lowered when Labarre orders him away.

occurrences.title: Another Hearth, Another Refusal
occurrences.status: Finds brief comfort at the hearth, then carries away his belongings after a second expulsion.

occurrences.title: Stones and a Closed Wicket
occurrences.status: Drives the stone-throwing children off with his stick, then asks the turnkey for lodging in vain.

occurrences.title: A Lighted Family Window
occurrences.status: Offers to pay for soup and a shed, then begs for water as the householder threatens to shoot.

occurrences.title: Even the Kennel
occurrences.status: Crawls into straw seeking warmth, then retreats from the dog using his pack as a shield and his stick to hold it back.

occurrences.title: The Fields and the Breach
occurrences.status: Abandons his search for shelter in the fields and re-enters D—— through a breach after the gates close.

occurrences.title: A Door Still Untried
occurrences.status: Claims to have no money, accepts four sous, and admits he has not knocked at the house across the street.

occurrences.title: The Yellow Passport
occurrences.status: Announces his nineteen-year imprisonment and reads the warning on his passport, expecting another rejection.

occurrences.title: Sir, Not Thou
occurrences.status: Marvels at being addressed politely and explains the savings accumulated during imprisonment.

occurrences.title: My Brother
occurrences.status: Describes the chains and punishments, astonished that his host treats him as a brother.

occurrences.title: Six Settings for Three
occurrences.status: Takes the bishop’s right-hand seat and eats hungrily after the blessing.

occurrences.title: Baptistine’s Account of Supper
occurrences.status: Remarks on the poorer meal and recovers animation as his host describes work in the country ahead.

occurrences.title: Fifteen Sous at the Door
occurrences.status: Grows silent with fatigue and pays little attention to the visitor.

occurrences.title: Across the Bishop’s Bedroom
occurrences.status: Follows through the bishop’s room while the household silver is put away.

occurrences.title: A Bed Beside His Host
occurrences.status: Thanks his host, then abruptly asks how he can know that his guest is not an assassin.

occurrences.title: Sleep Without Undressing
occurrences.status: Blows out the candle through his nostrils and falls immediately asleep in his clothes.

occurrences.title: A Waking Before the Retrospect
occurrences.status: Wakes in the middle of the night after his first sleep in the guest bed.

occurrences.title: The Broken Window
occurrences.status: Smashes the pane, takes bread, and is caught with a bleeding arm after throwing the loaf away.

occurrences.title: The Fourth Line at Bicêtre
occurrences.status: Sobs while the collar is riveted and lowers his hand seven times as if touching the children’s heads.

occurrences.title: A Shoulder Beneath the Caryatid
occurrences.status: Supports the loosening caryatid with his shoulder until the workmen can arrive.

occurrences.title: Half Wages at Grasse
occurrences.status: Unloads bales, shows his passport, and protests the fifteen sous offered for work said to earn thirty.

occurrences.title: Free of the Galleys, Still Sentenced
Silver in the Dark
occurrences.status: Lies awake estimating the silver’s value, then sits up and silently removes his shoes.

occurrences.title: A Window and an Iron Tool
occurrences.status: Tests the unbarred window, studies the low garden wall, and takes an iron miner’s candlestick toward the adjoining room.

occurrences.title: The Cry of a Hinge
occurrences.status: Waits in alarm after the hinge squeaks and discovers that nobody has awakened.

occurrences.title: The Sleeping Face
occurrences.status: Stops by the bed, takes off his cap, and hesitates before the unguarded sleeper.

occurrences.title: The Unlocked Cupboard
occurrences.status: Opens the cupboard with its key, takes the silver, discards the basket, and flees over the wall.

occurrences.title: The Candlesticks Too
occurrences.status: Learns his host is the bishop, is released, and accepts the additional silver in bewilderment.

occurrences.title: A Charge Spoken Softly
occurrences.status: Cannot recall making the promise the bishop invokes and remains speechless under his words.

occurrences.title: A Morning Without a Road
occurrences.status: Walks without eating, retraces his own paths, and resists the unfamiliar emotions stirred by his host.

occurrences.title: The Forty-Sou Piece
occurrences.status: Pins the fallen coin beneath his shoe and frightens its owner into flight instead of returning it.

occurrences.title: Calling into the Empty Plain
occurrences.status: Recoils at the coin, picks it up, and calls Little Gervais’s name without receiving an answer.

occurrences.title: A Priest on Horseback
occurrences.status: Gives the priest twenty francs while asking after the boy, then declares himself a thief.

occurrences.title: At the Three Paths
occurrences.status: Calls for the child one last time, collapses on a stone, and weeps as he confronts the theft and the bishop’s mercy.

occurrences.title: A Bolted Door and an Open Window
occurrences.status: Bolts the door, extinguishes the candle, opens the window, and struggles to collect his scattered thoughts.

occurrences.title: The First Excuse
occurrences.status: Reasons that the mistaken identification has secured his future but finds no joy in his decision to do nothing.

occurrences.title: The Duty to Speak
occurrences.status: Decides to expose himself, burns debts owed by struggling tradesmen, writes to Laffitte, and gathers money and his current passport.

occurrences.title: Fantine in the Balance
occurrences.status: Lights a fire against the cold and imagines that abandoning his public work would sacrifice many lives to save one.

occurrences.title: The Hidden Clothes Burn
occurrences.status: Destroys the hidden blouse, trousers, knapsack and thorn cudgel, then screens the empty cupboard with furniture.

occurrences.title: The Candlesticks Spared
occurrences.status: Stirs the coals with a candlestick, recoils at the voice of conscience, and returns both candlesticks to the chimney-piece.

occurrences.title: No Final Resolution
occurrences.status: Paces until exhaustion while the feared loss of either happiness or virtue defeats each apparent decision.

occurrences.title: Sleep at Three
occurrences.status: Drops into the chair and falls asleep after nearly five hours on his feet.

occurrences.title: The Dream of the Silent Men
Lanterns Below the Window
occurrences.status: Wakes beside the dying candle and spent fire, then recognizes the white horse and tilbury below.

occurrences.title: The Portress Waits
occurrences.status: At first denies ordering the carriage, then asks the waiting woman to say he is coming.

occurrences.title: A Collision Before Dawn
occurrences.status: Continues at speed after the wheel is struck, still without a settled decision about the trial.

occurrences.title: The Damaged Wheel at Hesdin
occurrences.status: Tries repairs, replacement wheels, another carriage, post-horses and a saddle before inwardly welcoming the apparent impossibility.

occurrences.title: The Boy Finds a Cart
occurrences.status: Pays for the old cart, leaves the tilbury for repair, and resumes travel despite resenting the rescue of his plans.

occurrences.title: Bread at Saint-Pol
occurrences.status: Guards the horse’s oats, accepts breakfast, then finds the bread bitter and leaves it almost untouched.

occurrences.title: A Road Barred Beyond Tinques
occurrences.status: Insists on reaching Arras that evening and asks the road-mender how to navigate the repairs and crossroads.

occurrences.title: An Extra Horse and a Guide
occurrences.status: Passes the road-mender’s position again at speed after obtaining help, conscious of the half-hour lost.

occurrences.title: A Branch for the Broken Whiffle-Tree
occurrences.status: Cuts a replacement whiffle-tree instead of turning back and realizes he never asked the hour of trial.

occurrences.title: The Truth and a Hopeful Guess
A Horse That Must Rest
occurrences.status: Returns the extra horse, stables the white horse himself, and refuses bed and supper.

occurrences.title: A Place on the Night Mail
occurrences.status: Shows his passport and pays for the available seat for the return that night.

occurrences.title: The Lights at the Prefecture
occurrences.status: Wanders through unfamiliar streets, asks the way, and claims he wants only to speak to a lawyer.

occurrences.title: The Wrong Finished Case
occurrences.status: Mistakes the completed infanticide trial for the case he came to see, then learns another hearing is still under way.

occurrences.title: A Name That Opens a Door
occurrences.status: Retreats to the landing, writes the name Madeleine with his office, and returns to demand the note be delivered.

occurrences.title: The Usher Returns
occurrences.status: Reads and crushes the president’s deferential note, then follows the usher away from the public entrance.

occurrences.title: Alone Before the Door
occurrences.status: Stands alone after the usher leaves, reads Pache’s framed letter without attending to it and begins to fear the brass handle.

occurrences.title: A Flight Reversed
occurrences.status: Flees the threshold, halts against a cold wall, and returns in anguish without being physically compelled.

occurrences.title: The Brass Handle
occurrences.status: Fixes on the polished knob and at last grasps it to enter the court.

occurrences.title: The Man on the Bench
occurrences.status: Recoils at the prisoner’s resemblance to his former self and sits behind boxes to watch without being seen.

occurrences.title: The Prosecutor’s Portrait
occurrences.status: Remains concealed among the privileged spectators while the demand for penal servitude is made.

occurrences.title: Champmathieu’s Own Account
occurrences.status: Hears the prisoner’s effort to account for himself from the place behind the judges.

occurrences.title: Two Questions, Still Denied
occurrences.status: Listens as the denial fails to overcome the alleged resemblance.

occurrences.title: Brevet Persists
occurrences.status: Hears his former prison companion identify another man in his place.

occurrences.title: Chenildieu Persists
occurrences.status: Watches the second former companion repeat the mistaken recognition.

occurrences.title: Cochepaille and the Last Murmur
occurrences.status: Rises, calls the three witnesses by name, and steps through the half-door into the hall.

occurrences.title: The Name Spoken Publicly
occurrences.status: Asks that Champmathieu be released and himself arrested, declaring his identity before the room.

occurrences.title: Proofs the Witnesses Know
occurrences.status: Admits both thefts and names Brevet’s suspenders, Chenildieu’s burned shoulder and Cochepaille’s dated tattoo.

occurrences.title: No Hand Raised to Stop Him
occurrences.status: States where the prosecutor may find him, walks to the door, and departs unhindered.

occurrences.title: White Hair at Daybreak
occurrences.status: Asks after Fantine, agrees she should not have been undeceived, and looks indifferently at his white hair in the doctor’s glass.

occurrences.title: A Question on Waking
occurrences.status: Draws the curtains, watches the laboured breathing, and stands silently by the bed.

occurrences.title: The Child Said to Be Here
occurrences.status: Cannot answer the first demand and later promises that Cosette is well and will be seen soon.

occurrences.title: A Voice in the Yard
occurrences.status: Holds the patient’s hand, listens anxiously, and hesitates to tell her what he came to say.

occurrences.title: Someone Behind Him
occurrences.status: Raises his head at the silence, questions the patient, and turns to see the inspector.

occurrences.title: The Triumph at the Door
occurrences.status: Meets the inspector’s eyes after the patient alerts him.

occurrences.title: The Arrest at the Bedside
occurrences.status: Assures her the inspector has not come for her, accepts the grip on his collar, and asks to speak privately.

occurrences.title: The Hope Taken Away
occurrences.status: Asks for three days to fetch Cosette and offers to be accompanied by the inspector.

occurrences.title: A Bar of Iron and a Farewell
occurrences.status: Accuses Javert, wrenches a rod from the old bedstead, tends Fantine’s body, and returns himself to the inspector’s disposal.

occurrences.title: The City Prison
occurrences.status: Enters the city prison in the inspector’s custody.

occurrences.title: A Hand at the Lodge Window
occurrences.status: Takes the key, lights the taper, explains his prison escape, and asks the portress to find the nurse.

occurrences.title: Evidence Left on the Table
occurrences.status: Identifies the relics from the fire, leaves them prominently displayed, and bundles the silver candlesticks in torn linen while eating bread.

occurrences.title: Instructions for the Curé
occurrences.status: Entrusts the disposition note to the sister and declines another visit to Fantine because it could bring the pursuit to her room.

occurrences.title: Two Answers for Javert
occurrences.status: Extinguishes his candle and hides in the angle screened by the opening door while the search enters.

occurrences.title: A Bundle on the Paris Road
occurrences.status: Departs toward Paris through trees and mist with a bundle and an unexplained change into a blouse.

occurrences.title: The Convict in the Rigging
occurrences.status: Obtains permission to attempt rescue, breaks the ankle-chain, climbs the rigging, and brings the sailor back to the main-top.

occurrences.title: A Fall Without a Body
occurrences.status: Falls from the lower rigging into the water and disappears from the watchers’ sight.

occurrences.title: Back into Paris
occurrences.status: Returns with the child, hires a cab to the Observatoire, and leads her on toward the Boulevard de l’Hôpital.

occurrences.title: Asleep with Catherine
occurrences.status: Recognizes her fatigue and carries her through the dark streets.

occurrences.title: Two Keys and a Waiting Fire
occurrences.status: Uses separate keys for house and room, lays Cosette in the folding bed, and kneels by her after kissing her hand.

occurrences.title: No Broom Required
occurrences.status: Smiles at her awakening and answers the request to sweep by telling her to play.

occurrences.title: A New Affection
occurrences.status: Keeps still beside Cosette’s bed at daybreak, waiting for her to wake and feeling his affection awaken.

occurrences.title: A Note in the Coat Lining
occurrences.status: Cuts open the coat lining and removes a thousand-franc note, unaware of the observer at the crack.

occurrences.title: An Explanation Repeated as Gossip
occurrences.status: Gives the note to be changed and describes it as quarterly income received yesterday.

occurrences.title: The Coat Examined Again
occurrences.status: Saws firewood in his shirt-sleeves in the corridor while the old woman examines the coat indoors.

occurrences.title: A Face Beneath the Lantern
occurrences.status: Gives the customary alms, recoils at a familiar-looking face, and returns troubled without asking a question.

occurrences.title: The Familiar Beadle Next Evening
occurrences.status: Returns resolutely, receives an ordinary thanks, and laughs away his earlier suspicion.

occurrences.title: A Light Through the Keyhole
occurrences.status: Stops the spelling, extinguishes the candle, sends Cosette quietly to bed, and stays awake after the listening light recedes.

occurrences.title: The Back at the Staircase
occurrences.status: Watches through the keyhole and recognizes the tall man’s neck and shoulders without opening his window for another look.

occurrences.title: Dumont, or Daumont
occurrences.status: Asks the new arrival’s name and occupation while trying to sound natural.

occurrences.title: A Coin on the Floor
occurrences.status: Rolls up a hundred francs despite a noisy dropped coin, surveys the street, and takes the child out.

occurrences.title: Circuits in the Left-Bank Streets
occurrences.status: Doubles back through the lanes and decides against returning to Gorbeau, without knowing a secure destination.

occurrences.title: Men Beneath the Lantern
occurrences.status: Sees three men pass beneath the lantern, one turning toward the police office, and hurries away with Cosette.

occurrences.title: Recognition in the Moonlight
occurrences.status: Waits in shadow and recognizes the leader’s face when moonlight reveals it.

occurrences.title: Toward the River
occurrences.status: Uses the pursuers’ hesitation to hurry toward the quay and briefly believes the empty streets mean safety.

occurrences.title: Two Sous for the Bridge
occurrences.status: Pays the extra sou, crosses in the cart’s shadow, and sets Cosette down when she asks to walk.

occurrences.title: Four Shadows Behind
occurrences.status: Looks back from the timber-yards, sees four figures entering the bridge, and chooses the narrow street.

occurrences.title: The Right Branch of the Y
occurrences.status: Chooses the less inhabited branch, carries the child, and discovers a man blocking the apparently open exit.

occurrences.title: A Net Closing
occurrences.status: Rejects the guarded exit and sees the dead end as a trap while fearing Javert behind him.

occurrences.title: No Way Through the Doors
occurrences.status: Rejects the broken pipe, barred windows and exposed climb, then finds solid stone behind the rotten wooden façade.

occurrences.title: A Rope from the Lantern
occurrences.status: Measures the wall, rejects carrying a burden during the ascent, and breaks the lantern-box latch to obtain its rope.

occurrences.title: A Name Used to Enforce Silence
occurrences.status: Claims Madame Thénardier is coming to take her back so that she will not cry out.

occurrences.title: Over the Wall
occurrences.status: Ties the cravat beneath her arms, climbs unburdened, hauls her up, and descends by roof and linden with her on his back.

occurrences.title: Hidden Under the Shed
occurrences.status: Puts his shoes back on, shelters with Cosette, and lightly covers her mouth while listening.

occurrences.title: A Hymn in the Darkness
occurrences.status: Kneels and loses awareness of the threatening night while the hymn lasts.

occurrences.title: Cold Beneath the Coat
occurrences.status: Realizes she has not slept, reassures her about his invented threat, and covers her with his own coat.

occurrences.title: The Motionless Form
occurrences.status: Tries the closed building, watches the still form through glass, and flees without learning whether it lives or dies.

occurrences.title: Back to the Sleeping Child
occurrences.status: Returns breathless, touches the stones to steady himself, and approaches the child.

occurrences.title: A Bell Among the Melon Beds
occurrences.status: Hears the bell, watches the moving figure, and hides Cosette behind disused furniture.

occurrences.title: Still Breathing
occurrences.status: Fails to wake her, fears she is dead, then rushes out to seek warmth and a bed.

occurrences.title: Father Madeleine in the Garden
occurrences.status: Offers a hundred francs for shelter and is startled when the stranger calls him Father Madeleine.

occurrences.title: Fauchelevent Recognized
occurrences.status: Recognizes Fauchelevent, questions him cautiously, and learns that the shelter is the convent where he obtained the old man’s post.

occurrences.title: A Life for a Life
occurrences.status: Invokes the old rescue and asks that Fauchelevent neither disclose what he knows nor investigate further.

occurrences.title: The Gardener’s Fire
occurrences.status: Recovers coat, cravat and hat and warms himself at the table with the old man.

occurrences.title: It Is My Turn Now
occurrences.status: Says he must remain and considers the refuge’s protection and danger.

occurrences.title: To Stay, First Get Out
occurrences.status: Sees a possible education for Cosette but recoils from returning to the watched streets.

occurrences.title: A Basket for the Child
occurrences.status: Accepts the grandfather cover and asks for an equally concealed way out for himself.

occurrences.title: The Gardener Is Summoned
occurrences.status: Watches the gardener leave after being told to remain concealed.

occurrences.title: A Brother and an Iron Bar
Instructions for Cosette
occurrences.status: Uses the threat of Madame Thénardier to enforce silence and again refuses to leave over the wall.

occurrences.title: A Living Substitute
occurrences.status: Volunteers to leave in the municipal coffin beneath the white pall.

occurrences.title: The Locked Nook and the Coffin
occurrences.status: Establishes the keys, route and timing needed to enter the coffin unseen.

occurrences.title: Air Holes and a Drunken Friend
occurrences.status: Specifies holes near his mouth and accepts the hearse as his only concealed exit.

occurrences.title: The Hearse on the Boulevard
occurrences.status: Travels concealed in the coffin being taken for a nun’s burial.

occurrences.title: Mestienne’s Replacement
occurrences.status: Remains hidden in the stopped hearse without hearing the change of plan.

occurrences.title: Business First
occurrences.status: Is carried toward the grave while still relying on the original rescue plan.

occurrences.title: The Journey Within the Box
occurrences.status: Tracks the journey through sound and motion and recovers from the coffin’s tilted descent.

occurrences.title: Prayers Through the Lid
occurrences.status: Hears the Latin service and assumes Fauchelevent will take Mestienne away.

occurrences.title: Earth on the Air Holes
occurrences.status: Loses consciousness after four shovelfuls fall and an air hole becomes blocked.

occurrences.title: The Offer to Pay
occurrences.status: Remains concealed beneath the falling earth.

occurrences.title: A Stolen Card and a Fine
occurrences.status: Lies unconscious inside the coffin after the fourth shovelful.

occurrences.title: A Face Mistaken for Death
occurrences.status: Lies motionless with closed eyes while fresh air reaches him.

occurrences.title: Fresh Air and Brandy
occurrences.status: Revives after fainting, drinks brandy and helps bury the now empty coffin.

occurrences.title: Two Men Through the Gate
occurrences.status: Walks out carrying the mattock and waits outside Gribier’s address.

occurrences.title: At Number Sixty-Two
occurrences.status: Returns with the child after leaving the cemetery.

occurrences.title: The Servant’s Door
occurrences.status: Crosses into the garden openly under the agreed cover.

occurrences.title: He Answers Well
occurrences.status: Remains entirely silent while the false identity is accepted.

occurrences.title: The Pavilion and the Rear Lodge
The Guard Under an Assumed Name
The Clothes and the Quiet Door
The Bread She Would Share
occurrences.status: Explains his self-denial and switches to white bread to prevent her sharing it.

occurrences.title: The Mother Whose Name Is Withheld
Through Martyrdom
occurrences.status: Answers Through martyrdom and delights in the child’s affection.

occurrences.title: What Is to Become of Me?
The New Clothes
occurrences.status: Praises her with bitterness and asks afterward for the former clothes to return.

occurrences.title: The Other Side of the Glance
She Walks Toward Him
occurrences.status: Accompanies her on the requested walk.

occurrences.title: A Return Without Marius
occurrences.status: Invites her back and is hurt when she declines another visit the next day.

occurrences.title: Daybreak at the Barrière du Maine
occurrences.status: Sits on the planks in reverie until Cosette calls attention to the road.

occurrences.title: What Those Men Are
occurrences.status: Recognizes his former route and answers that the men are convicts going to the galleys.

occurrences.title: A Festival to Dispel the Memory
The Question Remains
occurrences.status: Watches her tenderly before the remembered subject returns.

occurrences.title: The Gate Examined
occurrences.status: Grows anxious at the account and examines the gate closely.

occurrences.title: Three Nights of Watching
occurrences.status: Patrols the garden with a club through three nights.

occurrences.title: A Chimney-Pot Explanation
occurrences.status: Calls up to Cosette and shows the chimney-pipe shadow on the lawn.

occurrences.title: Reassured at Breakfast
occurrences.status: Shares the reassuring breakfast and becomes tranquil again.

occurrences.title: What They Have Told Each Other
Alone on the Slope
occurrences.status: Sits alone with his face shaded by a long-visored cap.

occurrences.title: Move Away from Your House
occurrences.status: Unfolds the paper and reads the instruction to leave his house.

occurrences.title: A Figure at the Moat
occurrences.status: Returns home in thought after springing up and seeing the figure escape over the parapet.

occurrences.title: Dinner and an Unheard Warning
occurrences.status: Eats a chicken wing and paces in renewed security without taking in the warning.

occurrences.title: Writing Restored in the Mirror
occurrences.status: Examines the reversed blotting impression and its readable reflection, then sinks into the armchair.

occurrences.title: The Luxembourg Youth Without a Name
Which Quarter?
occurrences.status: Asks about the fighting and goes bareheaded to sit on the stone post.

occurrences.title: Gavroche Breaks the Lantern
occurrences.status: Addresses the child and takes a five-franc coin from his pocket.

occurrences.title: A Gift Accepted
occurrences.status: Places the hundred-sou piece in the boy’s hand and denies trying to stop his lantern-breaking.

occurrences.title: The Letter Handed to Valjean
occurrences.status: Claims he is the person to receive the letter intended for Cosette and takes it.

occurrences.title: Chanvrerie, Not Saint-Merry
occurrences.status: Asks whether an answer should go to Saint-Merry and receives the correction.

occurrences.title: The Reply Read in Secret
occurrences.status: Lights a candle with trembling hands and unfolds the intercepted reply.

occurrences.title: Relief That Becomes Gloom
occurrences.status: Calculates that Marius may still be alive and considers keeping the note from Cosette.

occurrences.title: Equipped for the Markets
occurrences.status: Wakes the porter and departs armed toward the markets about an hour later.

occurrences.title: The Fifth Uniform
occurrences.status: Enters in National Guard dress, removes his coat and throws it onto the pile.

occurrences.title: A Welcome and a Warning
occurrences.status: Answers by helping the selected man put on his uniform.

occurrences.title: Javert Recognizes Valjean
occurrences.status: Watches Javert’s rebinding attentively from the threshold.

occurrences.title: A Mattress Needed
occurrences.status: Rises from the corner post at the order.

occurrences.title: Two Ropes Cut
occurrences.status: Cuts one rope with each shot and drops the mattress into the street.

occurrences.title: Across the Fire
occurrences.status: Crosses the exposed street, shoulders the mattress and places it out of the gunners’ sight.

occurrences.title: No Rebound
occurrences.status: Receives the defenders’ thanks after the successful placement.

occurrences.title: Two Helmets
occurrences.status: Reloads between two precise shots that remove the observers’ headgear.

occurrences.title: The Unanswered Question
occurrences.status: Does not answer the question.

occurrences.title: Fifteen Rounds Refused
occurrences.status: Shakes his head when offered fifteen cartridges.

occurrences.title: Work During the Respite
occurrences.status: Stares silently at the opposite wall.

occurrences.title: Valjean Requests the Prisoner
occurrences.status: Claims the requested recompense, sits by the captive and cocks the pistol.

occurrences.title: Over the Small Barrier
occurrences.status: Leads the hobbled prisoner with pistol in hand and helps him over the small works.

occurrences.title: Alone Beside Éponine
occurrences.status: Places the pistol under his arm and looks steadily at his captive.

occurrences.title: The Cords Cut
occurrences.status: Cuts the neck, wrist and foot cords and releases Javert.

occurrences.title: An Address Freely Given
occurrences.status: Gives his current name and lodging in case he survives.

occurrences.title: A Shot into the Air
occurrences.status: Sends him away, fires into the air and returns to the barricade.

occurrences.title: What Marius Hears
occurrences.status: Reappears after the shot with the words it is done.

occurrences.title: A Moment Behind the Corner
occurrences.status: Holds the unconscious youth out of sight, lowers him and assesses the blocked routes.

occurrences.title: The Loosened Grating
occurrences.status: Clears the stones, lifts the grating and lowers himself with Marius using elbows and knees.

occurrences.title: The Corridor Below
occurrences.status: Stands in the silent corridor and hears the battle as a distant murmur.

occurrences.title: The Blind Branch
occurrences.status: Feels the walls and paving before shouldering the youth again.

occurrences.title: Uphill to the Right
occurrences.status: Chooses the rising right-hand passage to avoid a crowded river exit.

occurrences.title: Beyond the Watershed
occurrences.status: Follows the wider passage despite the changed direction of the current.

occurrences.title: The Light Behind Him
occurrences.status: Turns back at the unexpected outline of his shadow.

occurrences.title: Still Against the Wall
occurrences.status: Stops close against the wall without understanding the patrol’s consultation.

occurrences.title: A Shot at the Vault
occurrences.status: Keeps still after falling plaster reveals the overhead impact.

occurrences.title: The Burden Grows Heavier
occurrences.status: Bends to protect his burden from low vaults and suffers a rat bite.

occurrences.title: Downhill to the Left
occurrences.status: Selects the broadest branch and turns left down the belt sewer.

occurrences.title: A Heart Still Beating
occurrences.status: Checks the heartbeat, bandages wounds and reads the body-return address.

occurrences.title: Toward the Fading Light
occurrences.status: Continues carrying the youth as traffic noise dwindles overhead.

occurrences.title: The Pavement Gives Way
occurrences.status: Feels mud replace the solid surface beneath his feet.

occurrences.title: Holding Marius Above the Water
occurrences.status: Raises the youth above the rising water and searches forward for support.

occurrences.title: The Other Side
occurrences.status: Climbs the surviving paving slope and kneels in prayer beyond the pit.

occurrences.title: The Exhausted Approach
occurrences.status: Stops for breath, then presses onward to the light at the outlet.

occurrences.title: The Locked Outlet
occurrences.status: Sets down his burden and shakes the immovable grating and bars.

occurrences.title: Thinking of Cosette
occurrences.status: Sinks beside the youth and thinks of Cosette rather than himself.

occurrences.title: Thénardier Unmasked
occurrences.status: Looks up from his exhausted crouch, recognizes the barefoot man and keeps his own face in shadow.

occurrences.title: A Murder Assumed
occurrences.status: Accepts the offered rope mechanically while refusing to confirm the supposed murder.

occurrences.title: All the Money and a Strip of Cloth
occurrences.status: Spreads his small change on the banquette and permits the search while shielding his face.

occurrences.title: The Gate Opened and Closed
occurrences.status: Shoulders the wounded youth with help and passes through the opened grating.

occurrences.title: Breathing on the Shore
occurrences.status: Sets the wounded youth on the shore, sprinkles water on his face and recognizes the man behind him.

occurrences.title: Recognition and a Favor
occurrences.status: Names himself, submits to the inspector’s grasp and asks help getting the wounded man home.

occurrences.title: The Pocketbook and the Coach
occurrences.status: Finds the address in the pocketbook and takes the front seat beside the inspector.

occurrences.title: Marius Brought Home Alive
occurrences.status: Supports the youth beneath the arms and checks that his heart still beats.

occurrences.title: The Inspector’s Wrong Announcement
occurrences.status: Stands behind the inspector and signals that the youth is not dead.

occurrences.title: The First-Floor Sofa
occurrences.status: Feels the inspector’s hand on his shoulder and descends the stairs.

occurrences.title: One More Favor
occurrences.status: Requests one instant at home before yielding to whatever the inspector decides.

occurrences.title: The Coach Paid Off
occurrences.status: Alights at the narrow street entrance and expects to be taken to a nearby police post.

occurrences.title: Go Upstairs
occurrences.status: Knocks at number seven, accepts Javert’s instruction and calls to the porter as he enters.

occurrences.title: No One Waiting Below
occurrences.status: Leans from the open landing window and is astonished to find that Javert has gone.

occurrences.title: A Package Under His Arm
occurrences.status: Stands apart near the door with a wrapped package and bows to the formal request for Cosette’s hand.

occurrences.title: Permission to Whisper
occurrences.status: Stands motionless behind the happy company, still holding the package and not speaking.

occurrences.title: Friends and Provision
occurrences.status: Remains silently behind the company with the unopened package as the grandfather speaks of poverty.

occurrences.title: The Book of Banknotes
occurrences.status: Breaks his silence, announces Cosette’s fortune and unwraps the banknotes on the table.

occurrences.title: The Name of the Street
occurrences.status: Says he does not know the name of that street.

occurrences.title: The Silent Benefactor
occurrences.status: Affirms their ownership of the money without identifying himself as the rescuer.

occurrences.title: Home with the Guests
occurrences.status: Receives Cosette’s smiles and the affectionate inflections of her childhood.

occurrences.title: A Smile Before Departure
occurrences.status: Answers that he is content and laughs for her.

occurrences.title: The Emptied Apartment
occurrences.status: Looks through the emptied rooms, then sets down his candle and frees his arm.

occurrences.title: The Inseparable Opened
occurrences.status: Arranges the tiny garments, remembers their winter journey and sobs over the bed.

occurrences.title: Twelve Hours Beside the Bed
occurrences.status: Remains alone through the winter night and convulsively kisses Cosette’s clothes.

occurrences.title: An Unnamed Visitor
occurrences.status: Requests a private audience and waits pale and sleepless among the remains of the feast.

occurrences.title: A Room Offered
occurrences.status: Hears the invitation after his sleepless night.

occurrences.title: The Uninjured Hand
occurrences.status: Removes the bandages, shows his uninjured thumb and explains why he avoided signing.

occurrences.title: His True Name
occurrences.status: Names himself and insists he is not related to Cosette.

occurrences.title: The Reason for Speaking
occurrences.status: Explains his attachment to Cosette and his refusal to keep a false name for his own happiness.

occurrences.title: A Pardon Refused
occurrences.status: Withdraws his hand and declines the proposed intervention.

occurrences.title: Cosette at the Door
occurrences.status: Shudders at her arrival and remains silent.

occurrences.title: A Kiss and a Dismissal
occurrences.status: Kisses her forehead and gives the smile she requests.

occurrences.title: The Secret Kept
occurrences.status: Weeps and begs that Cosette be spared the disclosure.

occurrences.title: Permission to Return
occurrences.status: Turns back at the door and pleads to retain some contact with Cosette.

occurrences.title: The Room Below
occurrences.status: Chooses to remain below and sinks into an armchair in exhaustion.

occurrences.title: An Embrace Withheld
occurrences.status: Remains motionless and refuses the invitation upstairs.

occurrences.title: Call Me Monsieur Jean
occurrences.status: Checks his familiar address and asks to be called Jean.

occurrences.title: A Moment of Familiarity
occurrences.status: Clasps her, gently removes her arms and apologizes for using thou.

occurrences.title: The Word Corrected
occurrences.status: Shows a flash of joy, corrects her and turns away to wipe his eyes.

occurrences.title: Why Live So Sparingly
occurrences.status: Questions their economy and recommends a carriage and household of their own.

occurrences.title: The Unlit Hearth
occurrences.status: Finds the hearth unlit, supplies a seasonal explanation and tells Cosette he said not to make a fire.

occurrences.title: Chairs by the Door
occurrences.status: Moves the armchairs back to the hearth and falls silent on hearing Cosette’s account of her husband’s question.

occurrences.title: No Chairs Left
occurrences.status: Offers contradictory excuses for the missing chairs and leaves without the old farewell.

occurrences.title: The Uneaten Plate
occurrences.status: Claims he has eaten, points to the empty jug and finally promises to eat the potatoes.

occurrences.title: The Bedside Consultation
occurrences.status: Receives the neighborhood doctor while remaining in bed and insists that he is in good health.

occurrences.title: Preparing with Failing Strength
occurrences.status: Dresses in stages, lights the candles and barely recognizes his aged reflection.

occurrences.title: Ink Revived with Water
occurrences.status: Recovers from a faint and dilutes the dried ink before taking up the pen.

occurrences.title: A Knock at the Door
occurrences.status: Stops writing, clasps his head and hears the knock while grieving.

occurrences.title: Father Again
occurrences.status: Sits up with trembling arms and welcomes both visitors in immense joy.

occurrences.title: The Whole Truth
occurrences.status: Explains that disclosure would have made separation harder and imagines the offered life.

occurrences.title: The Plea to Live
occurrences.status: Says he is about to die while delighting in Cosette’s voice.

occurrences.title: The Physician’s Answer
occurrences.status: Greets the doctor and continues gazing at Cosette.

occurrences.title: The Crucifix and the Letter
occurrences.status: Fetches the crucifix, recovers from a semi-swoon and explains his manufacturing profits.

occurrences.title: The Last Blessing
occurrences.status: Blesses the couple, explains the bequests and dies after resting his hands upon their heads.

occurrences.title: The Hearse on the Boulevard
occurrences.status: Accompanies the priest in the mourning coach.

occurrences.title: Prayers Through the Lid
occurrences.status: Responds to the priest during the burial service.

occurrences.title: The Hearse on the Boulevard
occurrences.status: Rides behind the hearse in the mourning coach.

occurrences.title: Prayers Through the Lid
occurrences.status: Recites the prayers over the coffin.

occurrences.title: Flowers for a Supposed Rendezvous
occurrences.status: Offers flowers to travellers and sells a bouquet to Marius.

occurrences.title: A Secret Carried Back from Montfermeil
A Visitor Questions the Latch
occurrences.status: Questions whether leaving the door unlocked invites misfortune.

occurrences.title: Breakfast at Voltaire
occurrences.status: Is introduced to Marius and receives an unexpectedly affectionate embrace.

occurrences.title: The Cavalry Advances
occurrences.status: Carries the Emperor’s attack order to the cavalry.

occurrences.title: A Coat Caught Near Genappe
occurrences.status: Catches the Emperor’s coat with Bertrand to detain him.

occurrences.title: A Prowler and a Distant Wagon
occurrences.status: Moves furtively among the fallen, repeatedly checking whether he is observed.

occurrences.title: A Hand That Closes
occurrences.status: Takes the glittering ring and laughs at the hand that clutches his coat before questioning whether the body is alive.

occurrences.title: A Rescue Mistaken for Charity
occurrences.status: Pulls the officer clear, strips the cross, watch and purse, then pretends the pockets were already empty.

occurrences.title: A Hand That Closes
occurrences.status: Has a hand projecting from the heap and briefly clutches the thief’s coat.

occurrences.title: A Rescue Mistaken for Charity
occurrences.status: Revives with a sword-cut face, offers the possessions already stolen, and believes the man has saved his life.

occurrences.title: A Late Beginning in the Mud
Orders Beneath the Elm
occurrences.status: Remains under fire and tells Clinton to hold the position to the last man.

occurrences.title: A Battle in the Dreamer’s Night
Candles at Two
occurrences.status: Is directly addressed by the drinking Grantaire.

occurrences.title: The Street Closes
occurrences.status: Cries out in alarm as the crowd rushes into her tavern.

occurrences.title: Fear and Drunken Display
occurrences.status: Takes refuge upstairs and mutters that the world is ending.

occurrences.title: Revenge at the Widow’s Expense
occurrences.status: Protests the loss of her table and recalls the fine.

occurrences.title: Under the Chestnut Trees
occurrences.status: Keeps beside Dahlia, using their contrasting beauty to set each other off.

occurrences.title: Dinner at Bombarda’s
occurrences.status: Sits with Listolier among the dinner dishes, glasses and bottles.

occurrences.title: An Adoration for the Table
occurrences.status: Laughs amid the table’s music and chatter.

occurrences.title: A Toast and a Mistaken Embrace
Restaurant Philosophy
occurrences.status: Declares Édon’s dinners better than Bombarda’s.

occurrences.title: The Men Take Their Leave
occurrences.status: Remains with the women after Fameuil’s solemn kiss and departure.

occurrences.title: Watching from the Windows
occurrences.status: Asks what the men will bring them.

occurrences.title: This Is the Surprise
occurrences.status: Learns with the women that the men have left rather than brought gifts.

occurrences.title: Laughter at the Table
occurrences.status: Calls it droll and joins the cheer for Tholomyès.

knownPersonLabels.name: The writer of the petitions
knownPersonLabels.reason: An attribution of handwriting and fictitious signatures, not a separately embodied stranger. The source identifies the writer as Jondrette; the item discovery records that attribution.
The chapter starts by naming Jean Valjean and explains his changed prison number.

knownPersonLabels.name: Ultime Fauchelevent
knownPersonLabels.reason: The reader follows Valjean through the convent admission and knows this is his cover name.

knownPersonLabels.name: Little Gavroche
knownPersonLabels.reason: The source chapter heading already gives his name before the opening description.

knownPersonLabels.name: Brigand of the Loire
knownPersonLabels.reason: The title is a hostile family description explained within the colonel’s biography.

knownPersonLabels.name: Laigle
knownPersonLabels.reason: Chapter 176 already explains Lesgle, Légle, Laigle and Bossuet as usages for the same man.

knownPersonLabels.name: Théodule
knownPersonLabels.reason: The narrator names the officer inside his first descriptive segment; Cosette does not learn his family connection.

reveals.title: Madeleine and Jean Valjean
reveals.evidence:
The reader has, no doubt, already divined that M. Madeleine is no other
than Jean Valjean.

reveals.title: The Name Spoken Publicly
reveals.evidence:
“Gentlemen of the jury, order the prisoner to be released! Mr.
President, have me arrested. He is not the man whom you are in search
of; it is I: I am Jean Valjean.”

reveals.title: Two Names Remembered
reveals.evidence: “Thénardier.”

reveals.title: Two Names Remembered
reveals.evidence:
“I shall not forget that name,” said the officer; “and do you remember
mine. My name is Pontmercy.”

reveals.title: Jean Valjean Was Not Dead
reveals.evidence: Jean Valjean was not dead.

reveals.title: Fauchelevent Recognized
reveals.evidence:
He turned. A ray of moonlight outlined his profile, and Jean Valjean
recognized old Fauchelevent.

reveals.title: The Borrowed Beggar’s Clothes
reveals.evidence:
“The suspected individual” did indeed approach Javert thus disguised,
and bestow alms on him. At that moment Javert raised his head, and the
shock which Jean Valjean received on recognizing Javert was equal to
the one received by Javert when he thought he recognized Jean Valjean.

reveals.title: The Price of His Son’s Inheritance
reveals.evidence:
The inheritance of Father Gillenormand did not amount to much; but the
inheritance of Mademoiselle Gillenormand the elder was considerable.
This aunt, who had remained unmarried, was very rich on the maternal
side, and her sister’s son was her natural heir. The boy, whose name
was Marius, knew that he had a father, but nothing more. No one opened
his mouth to him about it. Nevertheless, in the society into which his
grandfather took him, whispers, innuendoes, and winks, had eventually
enlightened the little boy’s mind; he had finally understood something
of the case, and as he naturally took in the ideas and opinions which
were, so to speak, the air he breathed, by a sort of infiltration and
slow penetration, he gradually came to think of his father only with
shame and with a pain at his heart.

reveals.title: The Neighbor’s Daughter
reveals.evidence:
Marius had lived in the house for a tolerably long time, and he had
had, as we have said, but very rare occasion to see, to even catch a
glimpse of, his extremely mean neighbors. His mind was elsewhere, and
where the mind is, there the eyes are also. He had been obliged more
than once to pass the Jondrettes in the corridor or on the stairs; but
they were mere forms to him; he had paid so little heed to them, that,
on the preceding evening, he had jostled the Jondrette girls on the
boulevard, without recognizing them, for it had evidently been they,
and it was with great difficulty that the one who had just entered his
room had awakened in him, in spite of disgust and pity, a vague
recollection of having met her elsewhere.

reveals.title: The Mother and the Younger Girl
reveals.evidence:
She seemed to be eleven or twelve years of age. On closer scrutiny it
was evident that she really was fourteen. She was the child who had
said, on the boulevard the evening before: “I bolted, bolted, bolted!”

reveals.title: Ask for Inspector Javert
reveals.evidence:
“By the way, if you have occasion for my services between now and then,
come or send here. You will ask for Inspector Javert.”

reveals.title: My Name Is Thénardier
reveals.evidence:
“My name is not Fabantou, my name is not Jondrette, my name is
Thénardier. I am the inn-keeper of Montfermeil! Do you understand?
Thénardier! Now do you know me?”

reveals.title: The Waterloo Boast and the Painted Relic
reveals.evidence:
Who has not remarked the fact that odious creatures possess a
susceptibility of their own, that monsters are ticklish! At this word
“villain,” the female Thénardier sprang from the bed, Thénardier
grasped his chair as though he were about to crush it in his hands.
“Don’t you stir!” he shouted to his wife; and, turning to M. Leblanc:—

reveals.title: The Window Attempt
reveals.evidence:
One of the “chimney-builders,” whose smirched face was lighted up by
the candle, and in whom Marius recognized, in spite of his daubing,
Panchaud, alias Printanier, alias Bigrenaille, lifted above M.
Leblanc’s head a sort of bludgeon made of two balls of lead, at the two
ends of a bar of iron.

reveals.title: Do Not Hurt Him
reveals.evidence:
“Babet,” said Thénardier in a low tone to the man with the cudgel, “why
did you bring so many; they were not needed.”

reveals.title: Do Not Hurt Him
reveals.evidence: “Is Boulatruelle dead?”

reveals.title: Éponine’s Handwriting
reveals.evidence: “It’s in Éponine’s handwriting. The devil!”

reveals.title: Why Javert Did Not Wait
reveals.evidence:
At nightfall, Javert had posted his men and had gone into ambush
himself between the trees of the Rue de la Barrière-des-Gobelins which
faced the Gorbeau house, on the other side of the boulevard. He had
begun operations by opening “his pockets,” and dropping into it the two
young girls who were charged with keeping a watch on the approaches to
the den. But he had only “caged” Azelma. As for Éponine, she was not at
her post, she had disappeared, and he had not been able to seize her.
Then Javert had made a point and had bent his ear to waiting for the
signal agreed upon. The comings and goings of the fiacres had greatly
agitated him. At last, he had grown impatient, and, _sure that there
was a nest there_, sure of being in “luck,” having recognized many of
the ruffians who had entered, he had finally decided to go upstairs
without waiting for the pistol-shot.

reveals.title: Names Beneath the Masks
reveals.evidence: “Good day, Gueulemer!”

reveals.title: Names Beneath the Masks
reveals.evidence: “Your health, Claquesous.”

reveals.title: Names Beneath the Masks
reveals.evidence: “Good day, Bigrenaille! good day, Brujon! good day, Deuxmilliards!”

reveals.title: Éponine Finds Him
reveals.evidence:
“So I have met you at last!” she said at length. “Father Mabeuf was
right, it was on this boulevard! How I have hunted for you! If you only
knew! Do you know? I have been in the jug. A fortnight! They let me
out! seeing that there was nothing against me, and that, moreover, I
had not reached years of discretion. I lack two months of it. Oh! how I
have hunted for you! These six weeks! So you don’t live down there any
more?”

reveals.title: The Tenant Named Fauchelevent
reveals.evidence:
This unobtrusive tenant was Jean Valjean, the young girl was Cosette.
The servant was a woman named Toussaint, whom Jean Valjean had saved
from the hospital and from wretchedness, and who was elderly, a
stammerer, and from the provinces, three qualities which had decided
Jean Valjean to take her with him. He had hired the house under the
name of M. Fauchelevent, independent gentleman. In all that has been
related heretofore, the reader has, doubtless, been no less prompt than
Thénardier to recognize Jean Valjean.

reveals.title: The Two Boys Substituted
reveals.evidence:
Thénardier, to whom avatars were easy, seized this occasion to become
Jondrette. His two daughters and Gavroche had hardly had time to
discover that they had two little brothers. When a certain degree of
misery is reached, one is overpowered with a sort of spectral
indifference, and one regards human beings as though they were
spectres. Your nearest relations are often no more for you than vague
shadowy forms, barely outlined against a nebulous background of life
and easily confounded again with the invisible.

reveals.title: The Purse Surrendered
reveals.evidence:
Jean Valjean’s purse was of no use to M. Mabeuf. M. Mabeuf, in his
venerable, infantile austerity, had not accepted the gift of the stars;
he had not admitted that a star could coin itself into louis d’or. He
had not divined that what had fallen from heaven had come from
Gavroche. He had taken the purse to the police commissioner of the
quarter, as a lost article placed by the finder at the disposal of
claimants. The purse was actually lost. It is unnecessary to say that
no one claimed it, and that it did not succor M. Mabeuf.

reveals.title: Javert Names Himself
reveals.evidence: “Javert.”

reveals.title: The Voice at His Feet
reveals.evidence:
Marius bent hastily down. It was, in fact, that unhappy child. She was
dressed in men’s clothes.

reveals.title: The Voice at His Feet
reveals.evidence:
Marius bent hastily down. It was, in fact, that unhappy child. She was
dressed in men’s clothes.

reveals.title: The Intercepted Message Explained
reveals.evidence:
What had taken place may be related in a few words. Éponine had been
the cause of everything. After the evening of the 3d of June she had
cherished a double idea, to defeat the projects of her father and the
ruffians on the house of the Rue Plumet, and to separate Marius and
Cosette. She had exchanged rags with the first young scamp she came
across who had thought it amusing to dress like a woman, while Éponine
disguised herself like a man. It was she who had conveyed to Jean
Valjean in the Champ de Mars the expressive warning: “Leave your
house.” Jean Valjean had, in fact, returned home, and had said to
Cosette: “We set out this evening and we go to the Rue de l’Homme Armé
with Toussaint. Next week, we shall be in London.” Cosette, utterly
overwhelmed by this unexpected blow, had hastily penned a couple of
lines to Marius. But how was she to get the letter to the post? She
never went out alone, and Toussaint, surprised at such a commission,
would certainly show the letter to M. Fauchelevent. In this dilemma,
Cosette had caught sight through the fence of Éponine in man’s clothes,
who now prowled incessantly around the garden. Cosette had called to
“this young workman” and had handed him five francs and the letter,
saying: “Carry this letter immediately to its address.” Éponine had put
the letter in her pocket. The next day, on the 5th of June, she went to
Courfeyrac’s quarters to inquire for Marius, not for the purpose of
delivering the letter, but,—a thing which every jealous and loving soul
will comprehend,—“to see.” There she had waited for Marius, or at least
for Courfeyrac, still for the purpose of _seeing_. When Courfeyrac had
told her: “We are going to the barricades,” an idea flashed through her
mind, to fling herself into that death, as she would have done into any
other, and to thrust Marius into it also. She had followed Courfeyrac,
had made sure of the locality where the barricade was in process of
construction; and, quite certain, since Marius had received no warning,
and since she had intercepted the letter, that he would go at dusk to
his trysting place for every evening, she had betaken herself to the
Rue Plumet, had there awaited Marius, and had sent him, in the name of
his friends, the appeal which would, she thought, lead him to the
barricade. She reckoned on Marius’ despair when he should fail to find
Cosette; she was not mistaken. She had returned to the Rue de la
Chanvrerie herself. What she did there the reader has just seen. She
died with the tragic joy of jealous hearts who drag the beloved being
into their own death, and who say: “No one shall have him!”

reveals.title: The Pursuit Explained
reveals.evidence:
The reader has divined, no doubt, that Thénardier’s pursuer was no
other than Javert. Javert, after his unlooked-for escape from the
barricade, had betaken himself to the prefecture of police, had
rendered a verbal account to the Prefect in person in a brief audience,
had then immediately gone on duty again, which implied—the note, the
reader will recollect, which had been captured on his person—a certain
surveillance of the shore on the right bank of the Seine near the
Champs-Élysées, which had, for some time past, aroused the attention of
the police. There he had caught sight of Thénardier and had followed
him. The reader knows the rest.

reveals.title: A Package Under His Arm
reveals.evidence:
With Cosette, and behind her, there had entered a man with white hair
who was grave yet smiling, though with a vague and heartrending smile.
It was “Monsieur Fauchelevent”; it was Jean Valjean.

reveals.title: The Forest Deposit Explained
reveals.evidence:
The reader has, no doubt, understood, without necessitating a lengthy
explanation, that Jean Valjean, after the Champmathieu affair, had been
able, thanks to his first escape of a few days’ duration, to come to
Paris and to withdraw in season, from the hands of Laffitte, the sum
earned by him, under the name of Monsieur Madeleine, at
Montreuil-sur-Mer; and that fearing that he might be recaptured,—which
eventually happened—he had buried and hidden that sum in the forest of
Montfermeil, in the locality known as the Blaru-bottom. The sum, six
hundred and thirty thousand francs, all in bank-bills, was not very
bulky, and was contained in a box; only, in order to preserve the box
from dampness, he had placed it in a coffer filled with chestnut
shavings. In the same coffer he had placed his other treasures, the
Bishop’s candlesticks. It will be remembered that he had carried off
the candlesticks when he made his escape from Montreuil-sur-Mer. The
man seen one evening for the first time by Boulatruelle, was Jean
Valjean. Later on, every time that Jean Valjean needed money, he went
to get it in the Blaru-bottom. Hence the absences which we have
mentioned. He had a pickaxe somewhere in the heather, in a hiding-place
known to himself alone. When he beheld Marius convalescent, feeling
that the hour was at hand, when that money might prove of service, he
had gone to get it; it was he again, whom Boulatruelle had seen in the
woods, but on this occasion, in the morning instead of in the evening.
Boulatreulle inherited his pickaxe.

reveals.title: A Name on the Carnival Cart
reveals.evidence: “That don’t matter. You must try. You understand me, Azelma.”

reveals.title: What the Visitor Has Learned
reveals.evidence:
However, through his daughter Azelma, who had started on the scent of
the married pair on the 16th of February, and through his own personal
researches, he had succeeded in learning many things, and, from the
depths of his own gloom, he had contrived to grasp more than one
mysterious clew. He had discovered, by dint of industry, or, at least,
by dint of induction, he had guessed who the man was whom he had
encountered on a certain day in the Grand Sewer. From the man he had
easily reached the name. He knew that Madame la Baronne Pontmercy was
Cosette. But he meant to be discreet in that quarter.

stateChanges.title: The Last Request
stateChanges.evidence:
When the Bishop raised his head again, the face of the conventionary
had become august. He had just expired.

stateChanges.title: An Ant Underfoot
stateChanges.evidence:
Why not mention these almost divinely childish sayings of kindness?
Puerile they may be; but these sublime puerilities were peculiar to
Saint Francis d’Assisi and of Marcus Aurelius. One day he sprained his
ankle in his effort to avoid stepping on an ant. Thus lived this just
man. Sometimes he fell asleep in his garden, and then there was nothing
more venerable possible.

stateChanges.title: The Broken Window
stateChanges.injury: arm bleeding from the broken bakery window
stateChanges.evidence:
One Sunday evening, Maubert Isabeau, the baker on the Church Square at
Faverolles, was preparing to go to bed, when he heard a violent blow on
the grated front of his shop. He arrived in time to see an arm passed
through a hole made by a blow from a fist, through the grating and the
glass. The arm seized a loaf of bread and carried it off. Isabeau ran
out in haste; the robber fled at the full speed of his legs. Isabeau
ran after him and stopped him. The thief had flung away the loaf, but
his arm was still bleeding. It was Jean Valjean.

stateChanges.title: The Bloody Smile
stateChanges.injury: two upper front teeth extracted; bloody saliva at the lips
stateChanges.evidence: The two teeth had been extracted.

stateChanges.title: A Promise to Mother and Child
stateChanges.condition: faints after the assurance of help
stateChanges.evidence: Then she fainted.

stateChanges.title: A Night in the Infirmary
stateChanges.evidence:
M. Madeleine had Fantine removed to that infirmary which he had
established in his own house. He confided her to the sisters, who put
her to bed. A burning fever had come on. She passed a part of the night
in delirium and raving. At length, however, she fell asleep.

stateChanges.title: The Hope Taken Away
stateChanges.evidence: She was dead.

stateChanges.title: A Rescue Mistaken for Charity
stateChanges.condition: opens his eyes and revives after being freed from beneath the bodies
stateChanges.evidence:
When he had arrived at this stage of succor which he was administering
to this dying man, the officer opened his eyes.

stateChanges.title: The Last Half-Glass
stateChanges.injury: black eye from Madame Thénardier’s earlier blow
stateChanges.evidence:
Cosette was meditating sadly; for, although she was only eight years
old, she had already suffered so much that she reflected with the
lugubrious air of an old woman. Her eye was black in consequence of a
blow from Madame Thénardier’s fist, which caused the latter to remark
from time to time, “How ugly she is with her fist-blow on her eye!”

stateChanges.title: Over the Wall
stateChanges.injury: hands slightly abraded during the wall escape
stateChanges.evidence:
Jean Valjean allowed himself to slide down the roof, still holding fast
to Cosette, reached the linden-tree, and leaped to the ground. Whether
from terror or courage, Cosette had not breathed a sound, though her
hands were a little abraded.

stateChanges.title: Back to the Sleeping Child
stateChanges.evidence:
Cold, anxiety, uneasiness, the emotions of the night, had given him a
genuine fever, and all these ideas were clashing together in his brain.

stateChanges.title: Earth on the Air Holes
stateChanges.evidence:
There are things which are too strong for the strongest man. Jean
Valjean lost consciousness.

stateChanges.title: Fresh Air and Brandy
stateChanges.evidence: Jean Valjean had merely fainted. The fresh air had revived him.

stateChanges.title: A Stranger Beside His Father
stateChanges.evidence:
The colonel had been attacked by brain fever three days previously. As
he had a foreboding of evil at the very beginning of his illness, he
had written to M. Gillenormand to demand his son. The malady had grown
worse. On the very evening of Marius’ arrival at Vernon, the colonel
had had an attack of delirium; he had risen from his bed, in spite of
the servant’s efforts to prevent him, crying: “My son is not coming! I
shall go to meet him!” Then he ran out of his room and fell prostrate
on the floor of the antechamber. He had just expired.

stateChanges.title: The Cost of the Broken Pane
stateChanges.injury: Bleeding hand and wrist after breaking the pane
stateChanges.evidence:
The younger daughter exhibited her bleeding fist, without quitting the
corner in which she was cowering. She had wounded herself while
breaking the window; she went off, near her mother’s pallet and wept
silently.

stateChanges.title: A Burn Instead of an Answer
stateChanges.injury: Severe burn from the glowing chisel on his arm
stateChanges.evidence:
The crackling of the burning flesh became audible, and the odor
peculiar to chambers of torture filled the hovel.

stateChanges.title: The Porter Refuses
stateChanges.evidence:
The old man fell back without a sigh. The candle fell and was
extinguished, and nothing more was to be seen except a motionless head
lying on the sill of the small window, and a little whitish smoke which
floated off towards the roof.

stateChanges.title: One Minute
stateChanges.evidence:
Enjolras straightened himself up, and cast a convinced and severe
glance around him. Then he spurned the corpse with his foot and said:—

stateChanges.title: The Bloodied Coat
stateChanges.evidence:
Enjolras bent down, raised the old man’s head, and fierce as he was, he
kissed him on the brow, then, throwing wide his arms, and handling this
dead man with tender precaution, as though he feared to hurt it, he
removed his coat, showed the bloody holes in it to all, and said:—

stateChanges.title: Bahorel Falls, the Gun Fails
stateChanges.evidence:
Bahorel dashed upon the first municipal guard who was entering, and
killed him on the spot with a blow from his gun; the second killed
Bahorel with a blow from his bayonet. Another had already overthrown
Courfeyrac, who was shouting: “Follow me!” The largest of all, a sort
of colossus, marched on Gavroche with his bayonet fixed. The urchin
took in his arms Javert’s immense gun, levelled it resolutely at the
giant, and fired. No discharge followed. Javert’s gun was not loaded.
The municipal guard burst into a laugh and raised his bayonet at the
child.

stateChanges.title: A Hand Across the Muzzle
stateChanges.injury: Gunshot through the hand while blocking a muzzle aimed at Marius; any further wound remains uncertain here.
stateChanges.evidence:
As he turned half round, gazing in that direction, a soldier took aim
at him. At the moment when the soldier was sighting Marius, a hand was
laid on the muzzle of the gun and obstructed it. This was done by some
one who had darted forward,—the young workman in velvet trousers. The
shot sped, traversed the hand and possibly, also, the workman, since he
fell, but the ball did not strike Marius. All this, which was rather to
be apprehended than seen through the smoke, Marius, who was entering
the tap-room, hardly noticed. Still, he had, in a confused way,
perceived that gun-barrel aimed at him, and the hand which had blocked
it, and he had heard the discharge. But in moments like this, the
things which one sees vacillate and are precipitated, and one pauses
for nothing. One feels obscurely impelled towards more darkness still,
and all is cloud.

stateChanges.title: The Bullet’s Path
stateChanges.injury: Bullet pierced her hand and body, exiting through her back; she remains bleeding and cannot be moved without pain.
stateChanges.evidence:
“The bullet traversed my hand, but it came out through my back. It is
useless to remove me from this spot. I will tell you how you can care
for me better than any surgeon. Sit down near me on this stone.”

stateChanges.title: A Little Bit in Love
stateChanges.evidence: She tried to smile once more and expired.

stateChanges.title: The Young Artilleryman
stateChanges.evidence:
At the same moment, he pressed the trigger of his rifle. The flame
leaped forth. The artillery-man turned round twice, his arms extended
in front of him, his head uplifted, as though for breath, then he fell
with his side on the gun, and lay there motionless. They could see his
back, from the centre of which there flowed directly a stream of blood.
The ball had traversed his breast from side to side. He was dead.

stateChanges.title: The First Hit
stateChanges.injury: Struck by a bullet, falls and sits up with blood streaking his face, still conscious and singing.
stateChanges.evidence:
One bullet, however, better aimed or more treacherous than the rest,
finally struck the will-o’-the-wisp of a child. Gavroche was seen to
stagger, then he sank to the earth. The whole barricade gave vent to a
cry; but there was something of Antæus in that pygmy; for the gamin to
touch the pavement is the same as for the giant to touch the earth;
Gavroche had fallen only to rise again; he remained in a sitting
posture, a long thread of blood streaked his face, he raised both arms
in the air, glanced in the direction whence the shot had come, and
began to sing:

stateChanges.title: The Song Ends
stateChanges.evidence:
He did not finish. A second bullet from the same marksman stopped him
short. This time he fell face downward on the pavement, and moved no
more. This grand little soul had taken its flight.

stateChanges.title: The Child and the Basket Brought Back
stateChanges.injury: Bullet grazed his head while lifting Gavroche; Courfeyrac bandages his brow with a cravat.
stateChanges.evidence:
At the moment when he had stooped to lift Gavroche, a bullet had grazed
his head; he had not noticed it.

stateChanges.title: Four Friends Killed
stateChanges.evidence:
Bossuet was killed; Feuilly was killed; Courfeyrac was killed;
Combeferre, transfixed by three blows from a bayonet in the breast at
the moment when he was lifting up a wounded soldier, had only time to
cast a glance to heaven when he expired.

stateChanges.evidence:

Combeferre, transfixed by three blows from a bayonet in the breast at
the moment when he was lifting up a wounded soldier, had only time to
cast a glance to heaven when he expired.
